name: ema_crossover
prompt: Build me an agent that buys 10 RELIANCE when its daily 50 EMA crosses above its daily 200 EMA, and sells the entire holding when 50 EMA crosses back below 200 EMA. Automatic execution.
response:
I've drafted the workflow. Review and activate from the LogicCard — it will run automatically when the triggers fire.

Workflow summary
- Name: REliance 50/200 EMA crossover — buy on golden cross, sell on death cross
- Description: Buy 10 RELIANCE when daily 50 EMA crosses above daily 200 EMA; sell entire holding when 50 EMA crosses below 200 EMA. Automatic execution.

Steps (two branches)
1) Buy branch
- Trigger: daily 50 EMA crosses above 200 EMA on RELIANCE
- Action: place market buy for 10 RELIANCE (auto-execute)

2) Sell branch
- Trigger: daily 50 EMA crosses below 200 EMA on RELIANCE
- Fetch: portfolio (to read current holding)
- Action: place market sell for the entire RELIANCE holding (quantity resolved at runtime), auto-execute

Rationale
- Standard two-branch EMA crossover workflow: golden cross buys a fixed size; death cross exits the full position automatically.

Notes & caveats
- Indicator triggers use daily candles (not intraday). The workflow fires when the daily close produces the crossover.
- Sell step sells the current holding quantity at the time the sell branch runs — if you have no holding, the sell will be skipped/produce no order.
- No approval required; change to require approval if you prefer a manual confirmation step.

This is automation of your instructions, not financial advice.

That request doesn't fit Pivot's trigger types — they need a fixed price level or a fixed indicator threshold (RSI < 30, EMA cross, etc.). Two ways to express what you want:

name: sector_rotation
prompt: Every first Monday of the month at 09:30, sell my entire IT sector holdings and buy the top 5 banking sector stocks equally with the proceeds. Automatic execution.
response:
I've drafted the workflow for you: "Monthly IT→Banking rotation".

Summary
- Schedule: first Monday of each month, 09:30 IST (implemented as market open +15 minutes).
- Steps:
  1. Trigger at market open (+15 min) on Mondays.
  2. Fetch current portfolio.
  3. Screen top 5 banking stocks by market cap.
  4. Check for IT holdings.
  5. Sell IT holdings.
  6. Refresh portfolio.
  7. Allocate available cash equally across the top 5 banking stocks (market orders).
- Execution: automatic (no approval required).

Rationale
- Sells IT holdings first, then uses the resulting buying power to buy the bank stocks equally; fetches portfolio before and after sells to compute available cash.

Next steps
